subject: grill: interactive patching of a user model for the current task
body: New: autoresearch/taste/grill.py (+ .claude/skills/grill-usermodel, docs/grill.md). It works like grill-me. It asks the person about the current task's D1-D6 decisions one at a time, least-certain first, and shows the user model's guess as the recommended answer. Disagreements and stated reasons open depth-first follow-ups: an LLM writes them in the terminal, the agent writes them in chat via 'add'. Questions come from runs/<run>/decisions.jsonl, the trade-off bank or an LLM. Answers go to data/researchers/<slug>/grill/<task>/, outside every trackp split. 'apply' rebuilds usermodel.json from usermodel.base.json plus task-scoped principles (the person's own words) and exemplars (retrieval_pool for m5-m7, exemplars for m1-m3); m0/m4 refuse; m7 notes stale calibration; 'revert' undoes it. Interfaces touched: none (load_model reads the patched file unchanged). WS D note: a patched model is recorded in artifacts.metadata.grill, and advisor.history_text does not read grill answers, so R1 vs R1-prompt differ by more than the method when a patch is applied. No paid calls made.
